title: Equivariant finite covers splitting prescribed finite etale residue schemes
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and let a finite group $H$ act on $k$ and $S$ compatibly; the actions need not be faithful. Let $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ be finitely many points of $S$, and for each $i$ let $E_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$ be a finite etale scheme. There exist a finite group $J$, a surjection $\rho:J\twoheadrightarrow H$, a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ with a compatible $J$-action, and a finite surjective generically etale morphism $a:W\to S$, equivariant through $\rho$, such that, for $N=\ker\rho$,
$$k(W)^N=k(S).$$
For every $i$ and every point $w\in W$ above $s_i$, the scheme $E_i\times_{\kappa(s_i)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$ is isomorphic over $\kappa(w)$ to a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$. Empty $E_i$ and the empty list of points are allowed. Generically etale means etale over a dense open of $S$. The action on $k$ on the output is the original one composed with $\rho$. Normal means that the local rings are integrally closed domains; $k(S)$ and $k(W)$ are the residue fields of the generic points; and the superscript $N$ denotes the subfield fixed by every element of $N$.

The notions of field, integral scheme, projectivity, finite type, finite morphism, surjectivity, etaleness, residue field, function field and fibre product are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-sc-function-field] and [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Lemma 5.6, printed p.614, and Situation 5.3, p.613; finite-etale residue-scheme formulation obtained by taking finite separable splitting fields of the residue algebras. Normalization of the output in its function field is included. Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: If the list of points is empty, take $W=S$, $J=H$, $\rho=\mathrm{id}$ and $a=\mathrm{id}$. Then $N=1$, and every assertion follows. Otherwise put $K=k(S)$ and $A_h=(h^{-1})^*$.

source.place: Lemma 5.6, printed p.614; assembly of the four extracted arguments.

proof.text: Apply the local residue-polynomial lifting lemma to each $(S,s_i,E_i)$. Obtain $R_i=\mathcal O_{S,s_i}$, $F_i=\kappa(s_i)$, $D_i=\prod_bF_{ib}$, a finite Galois residue splitting field $L_i=F_i(\alpha_i)$ with minimal polynomial $q_i$, and monic lifts $f_i\in R_i[T]$. Its generic algebra is a nonempty finite product of finite separable extensions of $K$.

source.place: Lemma 5.6, printed p.614; assembly of the four extracted arguments.

proof.text: Apply the equivariant Galois polynomial envelope to $A:H\to\operatorname{Aut}(K)$ and these generic algebras. It gives $M/K$ finite Galois, complete factorizations of all $f_i$ in $M$, and the finite group $J$ of compatible pairs with surjection $\rho:J\twoheadrightarrow H$ and $M^{\ker\rho}=K$.

source.place: Lemma 5.6, printed p.614; assembly of the four extracted arguments.

proof.text: Apply the semilinear normalization model to this $M$, $J$, $\rho$ and second-projection field action. Its normalization $a:W\to S$ is finite surjective and etale over a dense open; $W$ is normal integral projective finite-type over $k$ with the required equivariant action on $W$ and $k$. Under $k(W)=M$, the kernel fixed field is $K=k(S)$ by the envelope lemma.

source.place: Lemma 5.6, printed p.614; assembly of the four extracted arguments.

proof.text: For every $i$, apply integral-root residue splitting to this normalization, $D_i$, $L_i$, $q_i$, $f_i$ and its complete factorization in $M$. All the hypotheses are supplied by the local-lift and envelope lemmas. At every $w$ above $s_i$ it gives $L_i\hookrightarrow\kappa(w)$ and an isomorphism over $\kappa(w)$ from $E_i\times_{F_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$ to a finite disjoint union of rational points, including the empty case. This supplies the remaining clause.

lean.statement: theorem exists_equivariant_finite_residue_domination (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Scheme.{u}) (pS : S ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral S] [IsHProjective pS] [LocallyOfFiniteType pS] [QuasiCompact pS] (hnormal : ∀ s : S, IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk s) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] (σk : H →* (k ≃+* k)) (σS : H →* Aut S) (hsemilinear : ∀ h : H, (σS h).hom ≫ pS = pS ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (σk h⁻¹).toRingHom)) (r : ℕ) (s : Fin r → S) (E : Fin r → Scheme.{u}) (e : ∀ i : Fin r, E i ⟶ Spec (S.residueField (s i))) [hefinite : ∀ i : Fin r, IsFinite (e i)] [heetale : ∀ i : Fin r, Etale (e i)] : ∃ (J : Type (max u v)) (_ : Group J) (_ : Finite J) (ρ : J →* H), Function.Surjective ρ ∧ ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsIntegral W) (pW : W ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (σW : J →* Aut W) (a : W ⟶ S), IsHProjective pW ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType pW ∧ QuasiCompact pW ∧ (∀ w : W, IsDomain (W.presheaf.stalk w) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (W.presheaf.stalk w)) ∧ a ≫ pS = pW ∧ IsFinite a ∧ Surjective a ∧ (∃ U : S.Opens, Dense (U : Set S) ∧ Etale (a ∣_ U)) ∧ (∀ j : J, (σW j).hom ≫ pW = pW ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (σk (ρ j⁻¹)).toRingHom)) ∧ (∀ j : J, (σW j).hom ≫ a = a ≫ (σS (ρ j)).hom) ∧ (∃ ha : a (genericPoint W) = genericPoint S, ∀ z : W.functionField, (∃ b : S.functionField, (S.presheaf.stalkSpecializes (specializes_of_eq ha) ≫ a.stalkMap (genericPoint W)).hom b = z) ↔ ∀ j : ρ.ker, (Scheme.functionFieldAut (σW j.val)).hom z = z) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin r) (w : W) (hw : a w = s i), ∃ (n : ℕ) (ι : pullback (e i) (Spec.map (eqToHom (congrArg S.residueField hw.symm) ≫ a.residueFieldMap w)) ≅ ∐ (fun _ : Fin n ↦ Spec (W.residueField w))), ι.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun _ : Fin n ↦ 𝟙 (Spec (W.residueField w))) = pullback.snd (e i) (Spec.map (eqToHom (congrArg S.residueField hw.symm) ≫ a.residueFieldMap w)))
